episodes.name: The Bell of Bellingham
episodes.flavour: The village bell has not rung in a hundred years. The Moss King took the clapper to the top of the sunken tower. The party climbs to wake the bell.

scenes.flavour: The village of Bellingham is too quiet. The Elder shows you the silent bell in the square. 'Wake our bell,' she says. 'The Moss King stole the clapper.'

choices.label: Promise bravely
choices.text: Make a promise about the bell, out loud.
choices.example: We will wake the bell today, no matter what!
choices.onGood: The Elder smiles and hands you a map of the tower.
choices.onBad: The Elder nods slowly. 'Hm. We shall see.'

choices.label: Explain kindly
choices.text: Explain why the village needs its bell.
choices.example: The bell rings so that everyone knows it is time to gather.
choices.onGood: The Elder listens carefully and nods. 'Good reason.'
choices.onBad: The Elder frowns a little. 'The reasons grow quieter each year.'

choices.label: Ask a question
choices.text: Ask the Elder a polite question about the tower.
choices.target: A polite question with 'Could you tell us...'
choices.example: Could you tell us how high the tower is?
choices.onGood: The Elder answers with a story and a warning.
choices.onBad: The Elder gives a short, worried answer.

choices.label: Offer a gift
choices.text: Offer the Elder something from the party's pack, with one kind sentence.
choices.target: A 'please take this' sentence with an adjective.
choices.example: Please take this warm blanket for the cold nights.
choices.onGood: The Elder's eyes soften. 'Kind hearts travel far.'
choices.onBad: The Elder shakes their head. 'Keep it. You will need it more.'

scenes.flavour: A river blocks the way. A grumpy toll-keeper sits by a rope bridge, and he will not move for free.

choices.label: Ask politely
choices.text: Ask the toll-keeper politely to let the party cross.
choices.target: A polite question with 'May we' or 'Could we'.
choices.example: Could we please cross the bridge, kind keeper?
choices.onGood: The keeper shrugs and lowers the rope. 'Fine. Go on, then.'
choices.onBad: The keeper shakes his head. 'No sweet words, no crossing.'

choices.label: Make a deal
choices.example: If you let us cross, we will bring you a bell's tune.
choices.onGood: The keeper's eyes light up. 'A tune? Deal!'
choices.onBad: The keeper taps his coins. 'Not good enough.'

choices.label: Tell a joke
choices.text: Make the keeper laugh with one funny sentence.
choices.target: A funny sentence with a comparison.
choices.example: My hero is as clumsy as a goat in a rainstorm!
choices.onGood: The keeper laughs so hard he drops the rope. 'Go on! Go!'
choices.onBad: The keeper just stares. 'I have heard funnier bells.'

scenes.flavour: Inside the forest, a wise owl sits on a branch and will only let you pass if you answer well.

choices.label: Answer the riddle
choices.text: Answer the owl's riddle: 'What grows louder the more you take from it?'
choices.target: A complete answer with 'the more... the more'.
choices.example: The more you take from a hole, the bigger the hole gets.
choices.onGood: The owl hoots happily and points to a hidden path.
choices.onBad: The owl shakes its head. 'That is a hole, not an answer.'

choices.label: Reason aloud
choices.text: Explain your idea step by step to the owl.
choices.example: First we listen, then we think, finally we answer.
choices.onGood: The owl nods slowly. 'A clear mind. Pass.'
choices.onBad: The owl hoots once. 'Too many words, little sense.'

choices.label: Be very quiet
choices.text: Give one quiet, calm command to the party.
choices.target: A short command with an adverb.
choices.onGood: The owl is so impressed by the silence it flies away. 'Pass!'
choices.onBad: A twig snaps. The owl looks annoyed but lets you pass.

scenes.flavour: At last, the Tower of Echoes. The Moss King's guard — a golem of cracked stone — blocks the stairs. Only a strong heart and strong words can move it.

prompt.text: Tell the golem why the bell must ring again.
prompt.example: The bell must ring because the village has been silent for a hundred years.

scenes.onGood: The golem rumbles, confused, and gives you an opening.
scenes.onBad: The golem shows no mercy. It attacks!

talkDown.label: Talk it down
talkDown.text: Persuade the golem to step aside with one kind, clear sentence.
talkDown.target: A polite request with 'please' or 'could you'.
talkDown.example: Please let us pass, great golem — the bell must ring again.
talkDown.onGood: The golem blinks slowly, then bows and steps aside. No fight needed!
talkDown.onBad: The golem does not understand. It raises a stone fist and attacks!

scenes.flavour: High in the tower, the clapper hangs on a chain above a bottomless drop. One brave voice must guide the climber.

whenSet.flavour: The toll-keeper's rope is still tied to the tower wall. With it, the climb is easier.

whenUnset.flavour: No rope, no help. The climb is steep and the chain swings far.

choices.label: Order carefully
choices.text: Shout an order to the climber, using 'carefully'.
choices.example: Carefully grab the chain, and don't look down!
choices.onGood: The clapper is caught! The party races back down.
choices.onBad: The clapper swings away, but one brave jump still catches it.

choices.label: Encourage loudly
choices.text: Cheer the climber on with one strong sentence.
choices.example: You can do this, we are right behind you!
choices.onGood: Your words carry the climber up. The clapper is caught!
choices.onBad: The climber hesitates, then jumps anyway. Barely caught.

choices.label: Describe the plan
choices.text: Describe the safest plan in two clear steps.
choices.example: First hold the rope tight, then swing to the chain.
choices.onGood: The plan works perfectly. The clapper falls into your hands.
choices.onBad: The plan is close, but the clapper nearly drops. Still caught!

scenes.flavour: Back in the square, the party fits the clapper into the bell. The whole village watches in silence, waiting for one voice.

choices.label: Wish out loud
choices.text: Say one sentence to wake the bell and the village.
choices.example: May this bell ring for a hundred more years!
choices.onGood: BONG! The bell rings across the valley. The village cheers!
choices.onBad: BONG! The bell rings, a little off-key. The village cheers anyway.

choices.label: Shout the promise
choices.text: Shout the promise from the very first scene, all together.
choices.example: We will never let the bell be silent again!
choices.onGood: BONG! The bell rings loud and true. The whole class is the hero!
choices.onBad: BONG! The bell rings, a little shy, then grows stronger.

choices.label: Name the village
choices.text: Say one kind sentence about Bellingham.
choices.target: A sentence with an adjective before a noun.
choices.example: This brave little village deserves its bell.
choices.onGood: BONG! The bell rings, and the village smiles for the first time in a century.
choices.onBad: BONG! The bell rings once, then twice, then happily.
